statute: Hague Agreement Concerning the International Registration of Industrial Designs (Geneva Act 1999), administered by WIPO
title: Hague System for the International Registration of Industrial Designs (Geneva Act, 1999)
content:
The Hague System allows an applicant to register up to a set number of industrial designs in multiple member territories through a single international application filed in one language with WIPO (directly or through a national office, where the member permits).

Key mechanics relevant to Ayurvedic products:
1. Subject matter: industrial designs, such as the shape of a bottle, container, applicator or distinctive pack, not the formulation inside it.
2. Examination: each designated office examines the design under its own law and may issue a refusal; novelty and design-definition standards differ by country.
3. Publication and deferment: designs are published by WIPO, and many members allow deferment of publication for a limited period.
4. Practical link: an Indian design registration under the Designs Act, 2000 is a common starting point; check whether the target export country is a member of the Hague System before relying on it.

This is a short curated summary, not the treaty text.
